name: Eastern & Southern Ukraine (Steppe · Odesa · Black Sea Coast)

language.script_notes: Ukrainian Cyrillic with і, ї, є and ґ on official signage; Russian is widely spoken in daily life in the east and south, so commercial signs and informal writing can appear in Russian (using ы, э and ё) — a reason not to rely on vocabulary alone.

road_furniture.line_paint: As national; long, straight steppe roads with sparse markings.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national, including white-painted pole bases and roadside objects in national colours.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs on Soviet blocks; low-pitched metal or slate roofs on single-storey village houses.
architecture.wall_construction: Whitewashed single-storey mazanka houses (clay, timber and reed) in the steppe and forest-steppe; large Soviet panel and khrushchyovka estates in industrial cities such as Kharkiv, Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia; ornate 19th-century Neoclassical and Art Nouveau masonry in Odesa.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash with blue trim on village houses; grey industrial blocks; warm cream and ochre in Odesa's historic center.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Industrial-city Soviet estates, factories, mine spoil heaps (terrikony) in the Donbas coal region; Odesa's Neoclassical center and Potemkin Stairs; whitewashed village mazanka houses.

nature.vegetation: Sparse, dry steppe grassland and vast wheat and sunflower fields; few trees beyond planted windbreak lines; reed beds and lagoons along the Black Sea and Azov coasts.
nature.terrain: Very flat, open steppe stretching to the horizon, dropping to the Black Sea and Sea of Azov coasts; the Crimean Mountains rise in the far south.
nature.climate_signature: Dry steppe climate with hot summers — noticeably sparser vegetation and bigger skies than the forested north and west.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — region letters such as 'BH' for Odesa Oblast.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A high proportion of older Soviet-era cars and industrial and mining trucks; trams operate in several cities.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage dates mostly from around 2015 and is outdated; Crimea and parts of the east and south cannot currently be updated, and large stretches have little or no coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The same steppe extends across the border, with Cyrillic script, Soviet architecture and similar black-and-white guardrails and farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The letters і, ї, є and ґ appear only in Ukrainian; Ukrainian bollards are not attached to a narrow support pole; Ukrainian plates carry a blue-and-yellow strip and white-painted pole bases are common.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar steppe and farmland near the southwestern border and Danube region
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Romania uses Latin script and holey concrete poles; Moldova's plates and signage differ from Ukraine's, and Ukrainian Cyrillic is a reliable separator from Romania.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The east and south is flat, dry steppe with industrial cities and whitewashed villages; the west has Carpathian mountains and wooden churches, and the center is greener forest-steppe.
